h: Oral Torah Restores the Memory of Sinai

p: In the Pesikta on this haftarah:
"'I have not rejected them nor loathed them':
here He answered him on two,
and on two He did not answer him.
'And Tziyon said: Hashem has forsaken me,
and my Lord has forgotten me.'"
And after this it says there:
You have sworn by your fingers;
let my right hand forget,'" etc.
And afterward it brings in the Pesikta:
הֵשִׁיב אָחוֹר יְמִינוֹ (אֵיכָה ב, ג) וְכוּלֵּי
"'He drew back His right hand' (Eichah 2:3)," etc.;
except for the sake of Your right hand," etc.:
"'So that Your beloved may be delivered,
save with Your right hand and answer me'" (Tehillim 60:7);
אָמַר לֵיהּ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא וְכוּלֵּי
"HaKadosh Baruch Hu said to him," etc.:
"My right hand is held in pledge for you," etc.,
I forget My right hand," etc.
עַל פִּי מַה שֶּׁאָמַר בַּגְּמָרָא (בְּרָכוֹת ו, א)
according to what the Gemara says (Berachos 6a):
נִשְׁבַּע ה׳ בִּימִינוֹ (יְשַׁעְיָה סב, ח) וְכוּלֵּי
"'Hashem has sworn by His right hand' (Yeshayahu 62:8)," etc.:
'From His right hand, a fiery law for them.'"
And this indicates the Written Torah;
for it is found in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 30, 74a):
"'Let there be light': this is the right;
'and there was light': this is the left."
וְכֵן כָּתַב בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (חֵלֶק ב קסז, א)
And so it is written in the holy Zohar (II 167a):
for from the right issues the left," etc.
the aspect of the Written Torah,
the aspect of Torah she'b'al peh;
must be included within the right.
And so it is in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 20):
and from the left was given
And this is the meaning of
there was the aspect of prophecy,
which is like the Written Torah,
that it is the word of Hashem;
we are speaking of what was given to be written."
that is, it is plain to the eye,
that it is the word of Hashem.
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה
This is not so of Torah she'b'al peh:
although in truth it too is
the words of the living God,
that the sage innovates it from his own mind.
For this reason it is likened to dew,
of which it is not evident how
it comes down from the heavens.
And in Bavel there began the occupation
and make a fence for the Torah";
come from the Anshei Knesses HaGedolah,
more than You decreed upon me."
And this is called the aspect of "back,"
that it is the word of Hashem.
And this is the meaning of
that the essence of Torah she'b'al peh,
which is in the aspect of "back,"
in order to rectify the "much anger."
they would have been given only
the five Chumashim of the Torah," etc.,
כִּי בְּרֹב חָכְמָה רוֹב כָּעַס (קֹהֶלֶת א, יח)
"'for in much wisdom is much anger'" (Koheles 1:18).
because there is subjugation to the kingdoms;
evil is found among the nations,
עַל יְדֵי זֶה נִכְנָס גַּם בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל
through this there enters into Yisrael too
and for this the "much wisdom" is needed,
is also called by the term "enemy,"
and because of this Moshe called it "uncircumcised,"
And this is "He drew back His right hand
that it is from Hashem Yisbarach.
So too all the secrets of the holy Zohar
for the Holy Tongue is explicit
that it is the word of Hashem,
And Aramaic is called the aspect of "back."
although he lived after the Destruction,
since he arranged halachos in the revealed Torah,
arranged them in the Holy Tongue.
in which things were said in Aramaic
although it is in the revealed Torah
But the secrets of the holy Zohar
and this is "He drew back His right hand."

p: וְזֶה שֶׁאָמַר לָהֶם הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא
And this is what HaKadosh Baruch Hu said to them:
which is the Torah, called the right hand;
and this is "save with Your right hand and answer me."
And that is what it says,
"And Tziyon said: Hashem has forsaken me":
alludes to the aspect of the Written Torah,
the blessing over the Torah before it
"When I call the Name of Hashem,
which alludes to the middah of Malchus;
we call it Torah she'b'al peh."
And to this Hashem Yisbarach answered
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַב בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (חֵלֶק ג רצח, ב)
for they are attached to His very Name."
And similar is what it says,
which is called the Name of Hashem, as stated.
And it says, "But I will not forget you":
הוּא עַל פִּי מַה שֶּׁאָמַר בַּפְּסִיקְתָּא
this follows what is said in the Pesikta,
that HaKadosh Baruch Hu said to Yirmiyahu:
and likewise to the sons of Korach:
And this is what it says,
And it is found in the Midrash
(Shir HaShirim Rabbah, on "Let him kiss me"):
Torah study was implanted in their heart,
the yetzer hara was then uprooted from their heart,
is to make a person forget,
as a matter of course they would not forget.
the yetzer hara, to its place,
they went back to being forgetful.
And so it is written in this parashah,
after "And you will eat and be satisfied,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בִּקְרִיאַת שְׁמַע (שָׁם יא, טו-טז)
as is written in Krias Shema (ibid. 11:15-16):
"And you will eat and be satisfied.
Beware, lest your heart be seduced";
as the Sifrei on this parashah writes,
And here, where it is written "and bless,"
מִכָּל מָקוֹם כְּתִיב אַחַר כָּךְ (שָׁם ח, יא)
lest you forget Hashem your God";
the dominion of the yetzer hara,
it can still make a person forget.
"And your heart will be lifted up and you will forget," etc.;
for the beginning of the serpent's enticement,
"And you will be like God," etc.
For from this, that Hashem Yisbarach clothed
for the purpose of creating the world,
in a garment of kingship and majesty,
"Hashem reigns, He is clothed in majesty"
And this is the matter of the primordial kings,
and that is why it says,
"And your heart will be lifted up and you will forget."
And about this it says "But I" (Anochi):
at the time of Matan Torah,
so that it not be forgotten.
Since they will remember Hashem Yisbarach
as a matter of course "I will not forget you."
And this is the purpose of the exiles:
that Torah study be fixed in their heart
which comes to rectify the "much anger,"
which is the corruption of the serpent,
who wants only to make a person forget
and through the Torah she'b'al peh
so that Torah study is fixed in their heart,
And on Shabbos, at the second meal,
which is the aspect of zachor,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (זֹהַר חֵלֶק ב צב, ב)
and as a matter of course one merits
And because of this we say this consolation.
